newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 21.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.

- Disciplinary proceedings have been initiated against ""certain officials'' in the Department of Justice on foot of the failure to implement the government decision to delist a judge from the Special Criminal Court.
- Ireland's former prime minister, Albert Rynolds has described the results of his libel case against a London newspaper as ""unjust and immoral''.
- The British government is set to announce some concessions on the operation of prison regimes in Northern Ireland.

- The Irish Deputy Prime Minister Dick Spring and the Northern Secretary, Patrick Mayhew, met for several hours in Belfast on Thursday night but produced no fresh initiative to resolve the deadlock on decommissioning of arms.
- Bus and rail union workers are preparing for a national transport strike over management proposals to extend a cost-cutting plan for the state-run Bus Eireann.
- A liquidator has been appointed to insurance brokers Andrew Reynolds and Associates, which has collapsed owing creditors almost 1.5 million Irish pounds.
- A major report recommending substantial salary rises for the country's top doctors looks set to trigger intense public pay anger.

- A huge inventory of animals and goods was seized during an armed swoop on Wednesday on the home and equestrian centre of John Gilligan, a suspect in the murder case of Irish journalist Veronica Guerin.
- Ireland's billion pound tourism and food industries could be threatened by the nation's thoughtless litter louts, experts said.
- Irish Finance minister Ruairi Quinn is still pressing for cuts of around 270 million Irish pounds to keep next year's estimates on target and provide scope for a budget tax package.
